sections.html:
Frederick County is the northernmost county in Virginia. Its seat is Winchester, but Winchester is an independent city and sits outside the county's tax system even though the county wraps around it. If your house has a Winchester address, confirm which jurisdiction sends your bill before you call any office.

The county had 91,419 residents in the 2020 census and an estimate of 99,955 for 2025. It has 35,827 housing units, and 78.8% of occupied homes are lived in by their owners, so most sellers here are individual homeowners. Middletown and Stephens City are the two incorporated towns. Many addresses are in unincorporated places such as Kernstown, Clear Brook, Gainesboro, Round Hill, Jordan Springs, Lake Frederick and Mountain Falls, and those owners deal with the county for everything.

The real estate rate is $0.53 per $100 of assessed value, and mobile homes are taxed at the same $0.53. The county also posts a real estate calculator you can run with your own assessment, which is the easiest way to estimate a bill before you list.

Tax typeRate
Real estate$0.53 per $100 of assessed value
Personal property$4.35 per $100
County meals tax6.0%
Lodging tax6.0%

Real estate tax is collected in two halves, on June 5 and December 5. When the office is closed on a due date, payment is due the next business day. The Treasurer also offers a way to pre-pay real estate taxes if you would rather settle early. Call the Treasurer for the current late-penalty figure before you plan a payoff.

The Commissioner of the Revenue keeps a calendar of the other dates a homeowner can meet during the year.

  • January 1 to April 1: application window for elderly and permanently disabled tax relief, with April 1 as the deadline.
  • June 5: first half of real estate and personal property tax.
  • November 1: land use applications, with a late filing fee accepted through December 1.
  • December 5: second half.

Relief for 100 percent service-connected, totally and permanently disabled former service members, and for surviving spouses of armed forces members killed in action, can be filed at any time of year.

Start by calling the assessor at 540-665-5680. An owner can appeal when the error was made by the Commissioner of the Revenue, or when it is a factual error by others during a general reassessment. A disagreement over value usually begins with the assessor, who can walk you through how the number was set.

The county describes three routes.

  1. Assessor hearing at the County Administration Building, 107 North Kent Street, Winchester. Call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, to schedule. Hearing dates are published in The Winchester Star and on the county website.
  2. Written appeal by email, by letter, or on the Appeal of Assessment form, mailed to Commissioner of the Revenue, Real Property Tax Appeal, PO Box 552, Winchester, VA 22604.
  3. Further appeal to the Board of Equalization and then the Frederick County Circuit Court.

Ask the Commissioner's office when the next reassessment cycle opens and what deadline applies to the Board of Equalization. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 sets the court timing, and the court starts from the assumption that the assessor's value is right for real property, so bring comparable sales and photos of defects.

The Commissioner's Real Estate Division runs the agricultural, horticultural and forest land use assessments. The same division handles tax relief for the elderly and disabled, for disabled former service members, and for surviving spouses of certain persons killed in the line of duty. Its page also links to a Tax Sale Information Center.

If your parcel is enrolled in land use, ask the division what happens to the deferral when the property sells, and ask before you set a closing date. Rules on rollback and who pays can change what you net, and the program rules are linked from the division's page.

Rural sellers should also check the county home page for current emergency notices, since a posted wildfire or weather update can affect showings.

Unpaid tax on a Virginia house is a lien that ranks ahead of other liens. Virginia Code 58.1-3340 says the lien lasts until the tax is actually paid, that sale proceeds go first to taxes and levies on the real estate, and that penalties and interest count as part of the tax. Your share of the current year is prorated in the sales contract.

A deed also triggers the grantor's tax under Virginia Code 58.1-802. It is 50 cents per $500 of consideration, and the seller pays it unless the buyer agrees to cover it.

In practice the sequence is short:

  1. Call the Treasurer and ask for a written payoff that includes penalty and interest and says how long it is good.
  2. Give the figure to the title company or closing attorney.
  3. The closing agent pays the Treasurer out of your proceeds and the lien is cleared.
  4. Keep the paid receipt with your closing papers.

A little preparation saves time with the county offices. Pull together your latest tax bill, any assessment notice, the names on the deed and the parcel number. If the house is in land use or you receive elderly or disabled relief, tell the closing agent so the status is handled before the deed is recorded.

If the house is inherited, vacant, rented or needs repairs, a cash sale skips showings, listing prep and a buyer's loan approval. Cash Home Buyers can look at a Frederick County house as it stands, and the title company still pays any tax balance from the proceeds at closing. Whichever route you pick, get the payoff in writing first so you know what is left for you.

faqs.q: What is the Frederick County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.53 per $100 of assessed value. Mobile homes are taxed at the same rate.

faqs.q: When are Frederick County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 for the first half and December 5 for the second half. If the office is closed on a due date, the next business day applies.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute a Frederick County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the assessor at 540-665-5680. To schedule a hearing, call 540-722-8319 between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is Winchester part of Frederick County?
faqs.a: No. Winchester is the county seat but is an independent city under Virginia law, and Frederick County surrounds it.

faqs.q: When is the Frederick County tax relief deadline for seniors?
faqs.a: Applications for elderly or permanently disabled relief are accepted from January 1 to April 1.
